lane_title: Flexural-Hinge & Conductance-Trough Coupling with Dilatant-Strain Gate
hypothesis: Basement flexural hinge curvature (Laplacian + Hessian ridge of depth_to_base_surf) coincident with MT conductance-trough clay caps (Hessian trough of log cond_surf) and gated by active dilatant transtensional strain (shear * max(dilatation,0)) isolates concealed high-permeability geothermal conduit faults beneath alluvial cover where surface scarps are absent.
mechanism: Buried normal-fault monocline hinges produce sharp basement curvature under flat piedmonts; fault gouge seals with smectite clay producing conductive troughs; dilatant step-overs open permeability for geothermal fluids. Conjunction of hinge+ trough + dilate at 100-600 m scales captures blind basin faults; anisotropic strand smoothing along topographic strike enforces fault continuity.
named_non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan/Bonneville paleoshorelines (~1330/1555 m constant-elevation benches) and fan-toe radial onlap producing hinge curvature without dilatant strain or conductive trough continuity.
physical_signature: Laplacian and Hessian ridge/trough at sigma 1.0/3.0/6.0 px on depth_to_base_surf and log(cond_surf), gated by shear*dilate product, conjunction at p70, anisotropic smoothing sigma_along 2.5 px sigma_cross 0.55 px.
why_off_catalogue: USGS/INGENIOUS mappers require surface scarp (det_elev_slope high); buried intra-basin faults under 10-100 m alluvium lack scarps but generate basement flexure hinges + clay gouge troughs + active dilatation invisible to air-photo mapping.
difference_from_existing: First to combine depth_to_base_surf flexural curvature (Laplacian+Hessian) ∩ log(cond) trough (Hessian trough) ∩ dilatant shear product with anisotropic strand integration. DHTC used deep MT + basement steps; QTSK used cover-thickness decoupling; MVRD used magnetite polarity; CTRA used conductivity curvature + gravity step. No prior uses hinge+trough+dilate conjunction.
